title: New commercial property in Newcastle: plan your 2027/28 move
excerpt: Industrial units in Lambton, healthcare space in Hamilton and a CBD heritage refurbishment: three Newcastle projects to investigate before your next premises decision.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
If your business needs new premises in 2027 or 2028, it is worth looking at the development pipeline now. A proposed building, an available suite and a confirmed move-in date are different things. Early planning gives you time to compare all three with the space you already occupy.

This article looks at three Newcastle projects being marketed or described publicly in October 2026: industrial units in Lambton, healthcare space in Hamilton and a heritage refurbishment in the CBD. They offer different property types and tenure options. They are not a complete inventory of Newcastle's development pipeline.

Limited supply can affect negotiating conditions, but it does not establish that rents or prices will rise for every property. Early commitment can offer more choice; it does not guarantee a lower price or a better return. The useful starting point is a clear brief, an affordable business case and enough time to compare alternatives.

> **Lease ending in 2027 or 2028?** Now is the right time to plan, not panic. [Book a free Lease Health Check](/tenant-rep) and we'll map out your options.


## Why your planning window is 12 to 24 months, not 3

A lease expiry is a deadline, not the ideal starting point for a property search. The right lead time depends on the size of the move, approvals, fitout and the premises available.

A commercial move has a lot of moving parts:

- Working out your brief: size, location, parking, budget, growth
- Searching, inspecting and shortlisting
- Negotiating rent, incentives, fitout contributions and make-good
- Your solicitor reviewing the lease or contract
- Design, approvals and fitout
- Furniture, IT, signage and the move itself

Every one of those steps takes time. A 12 to 24 month planning window can be a useful starting point for a significant move, particularly where a new development or substantial fitout is involved. It is a planning guide, not a standard delivery period for every project.

Check your current lease for option and notice dates with your solicitor. Missing a contractual deadline can affect your options; the position depends on the actual lease.

**A simple rule:** if your lease ends in 2027 or 2028, or you know your team will outgrow your space by then, your planning starts this year.


## Opportunity 1: The Commonage, Lambton (industrial units for sale)

![Aerial render of The Commonage industrial units on Wyong Road, Lambton, Newcastle](/images/blog/newcastle-property-2027-2028/01-the-commonage-lambton-industrial-units-aerial.jpg)

**What it is:** Stage 1 of a strata industrial development at 43-45 Wyong Road, Lambton. Colliers is marketing warehouse and business units for sale. Confirm the full staging plan, unit count and current release with the selling agent.

**Who it suits:** Tradies, storage, warehousing, light industrial and creative businesses. Basically anyone who has outgrown the garage, the rented container or the back of the ute.

**Details in the public Colliers listing, checked 31 October 2026:**

| Detail | The Commonage |
|---|---|
| Location | 43-45 Wyong Road, Lambton (Stage 1) |
| Release | Stage 1; confirm current unit availability with the selling agent |
| Sizes | About 80 m² to 169 m² (total unit area, including mezzanine) |
| Advertised starting price | From $595,000 plus GST; obtain a current unit-specific price |
| Zoning | E4 |
| Completion | Obtain the current proposed programme and contractual dates from the selling agent |
| Selling agent | Colliers |

![Warehouse cutaway render showing ground floor storage and mezzanine office at The Commonage, Lambton](/images/blog/newcastle-property-2027-2028/03-the-commonage-warehouse-unit-mezzanine-interior.jpg)

The listing describes mezzanine areas, high-clearance warehouse accommodation and dedicated on-site parking. Confirm the exact specification, amenities, services, access and car-space allocation for the selected unit in the contract documents.

### Check how the unit will work for your business

The listing positions the development for owner-occupiers and investors, with warehouse, showroom and business-unit configurations. Suitability for a workshop, storage, creative business or another use depends on the individual premises, planning requirements and approvals. E4 zoning alone does not establish that every proposed use is permitted.

Compare usable ground-floor space, mezzanine access, loading, parking and travel requirements against your actual work. Buying your premises also commits capital and creates ownership responsibilities, so compare the business case with continuing to lease.

![Courtyard render showing roller doors, a ute and car parking at The Commonage trade units in Lambton](/images/blog/newcastle-property-2027-2028/04-the-commonage-courtyard-parking-trade-units.jpg)

### Things to check before you sign anything off the plan

Buying off the plan can be a smart move. It still needs a clear head.

- **The contract:** sunset dates, what happens if construction runs late, and what the deposit is held as.
- **Final areas:** check how the total area is split between ground floor and mezzanine. A mezzanine is useful, but it's not the same as warehouse floor space.
- **Strata costs:** ask for estimated strata levies and what they cover.
- **Ownership structure:** buying through a company, trust or SMSF changes a lot. Talk to your accountant and financial planner first.
- **Finance:** discuss funding, approval conditions and settlement timing with your broker or lender, and have your solicitor review the commitment before paying a deposit.

## Opportunity 2: Hamilton Healthcare Hub (medical suites for lease)

![Street render of Hamilton Healthcare Hub at 98 Donald Street, Hamilton, Newcastle](/images/blog/newcastle-property-2027-2028/05-hamilton-healthcare-hub-donald-street-render.jpg)

**What it is:** A purpose-built medical precinct at 98 Donald Street, Hamilton, offered for lease only. It's planned to bring pharmacy, pathology, radiology, GP and specialist consulting, and allied health into one building.

**Who it suits:** GPs, specialists, radiology, pathology, pharmacy, physio, psychology, dental, OT, NDIS providers and health administration.

**Details in the public leasing material, checked 31 October 2026:**

| Detail | Hamilton Healthcare Hub |
|---|---|
| Location | 98 Donald Street, Hamilton |
| Tenure | Lease only |
| Advertised suite range | Marketing description states approximately 66 m² to 1,510 m²; the listing summary shows 66 m² to 702 m². Confirm the actual available suite and area with Knight Frank |
| Car parking | 140 on-site spaces, plus patient drop-off |
| Rent and timing | Contact the leasing agent for current terms, proposed completion and access dates |
| Status | Pre-commitment leasing is being marketed; final design and accommodation are subject to landlord confirmation and council approval |
| Leasing agent | Knight Frank Newcastle |

![Aerial render of Hamilton Healthcare Hub showing Donald Street and Samdon Street frontage and car parking](/images/blog/newcastle-property-2027-2028/06-hamilton-healthcare-hub-aerial-render.jpg)

Ask for the proposed landlord works and shell specification for the selected suite. Confirm ceilings, air conditioning, services connections and power/data provisions in writing before preparing the fitout budget. Do not assume that a warm-shell label includes the same work in every development.

### Compare the premises with the needs of the practice

The public material describes an integrated healthcare destination with parking and patient drop-off. That makes access, patient circulation, the proposed mix of operators and the actual suite layout useful questions for an inspection and brief.

A marketing description does not establish suitability for a particular medical practice. Review the intended use, approvals, accessibility, services and fitout requirements with the relevant advisers before committing.

### What to watch with a medical pre-commitment

- **Incentives:** ask what rent-free periods or fitout contributions are being offered, their conditions and how they affect the total occupancy cost. Early commitment does not guarantee a stronger incentive.
- **Net rent vs what you actually pay:** confirm whether the quote is net or gross, the GST treatment and estimated outgoings. Include the complete agreed occupancy scope in the comparison.
- **Warm shell vs fitout cost:** medical fitouts aren't cheap. Budget for the fitout before you sign, not after.
- **Approval and delivery risk:** ask for the current approval position and have your solicitor review conditions, timing changes and remedies in the proposed agreement.
- **Your current lease:** line up your exit or make-good with your current landlord so you're not paying two rents at once.

> **Weighing up a new suite against staying put?** Run the numbers through our free [Lease Comparison Tool](/resources/lease-comparison). Compare up to three options side by side, including rent-free, outgoings and rent reviews.


## Opportunity 3: 364-366 Hunter Street, Newcastle CBD (heritage refurbishment)

**What it is:** Two adjoining heritage commercial buildings on Hunter Street being turned into contemporary commercial space, keeping the original 1921 facade.

**The details published so far:**

- About 1,234 m² over two levels
- Upgraded commercial tenancies and new shopfronts
- Lift and stair access, amenities and building services upgrades
- An eight-space car park
- Developer: Altim Property. Architect: Space Design Architecture. AVIDPM describes proposed project services including design management, approvals coordination and tender management.

Whether the space will be offered for lease, for sale or both is still to be confirmed, along with timing and pricing.

**Why it's worth watching:** A refurbishment with character features and proposed services upgrades may suit a different brief from a new industrial unit or medical suite. Ask about intended uses, access, services, tenure and delivery dates before treating it as an available relocation option.

## Lease or buy? A quick comparison

| | Leasing (like Hamilton Healthcare Hub) | Buying (like The Commonage) |
|---|---|---|
| Upfront cost | Bank guarantee or deposit, plus fitout | Deposit, stamp duty, legal costs, plus fitout |
| Monthly cost | Rent plus outgoings and GST | Loan repayments, strata levies, rates and insurance |
| Flexibility | Depends on the term, options, assignment and exit obligations | Sale or leasing options depend on market conditions, approvals, finance and any applicable restrictions |
| Property value exposure | No direct ownership of the premises | Capital value may rise or fall; ownership also brings transaction and holding costs |
| Control | Alterations depend on the lease and required approvals | Ownership can provide more control, subject to strata, planning, finance and other restrictions |
| Decision test | Does the lease support the business brief and total occupancy budget? | Does ownership support the business case after funding, transaction and holding costs? |

There's no one right answer. It depends on your cash flow, your growth plans and how you want to structure things. That's why your accountant, financial planner and broker should be part of the conversation early.


## What early commitment can and cannot achieve

New projects may be released in stages. Asking questions early can give you time to compare configurations, negotiate terms and coordinate the proposed premises with your lease expiry. Current availability, incentives and prices still need to be confirmed for the actual transaction.

Pre-committing means agreeing to lease or buy before the building is finished. A useful agreement needs more than an attractive opening price. Work through:

- Whether the unit or suite meets your measured brief and intended use
- The complete price or rent, outgoings, GST treatment and transaction costs
- What the landlord or developer supplies, and what remains in your fitout budget
- Approval, design-change, funding and delivery conditions
- Access for fitout, practical completion and the point at which rent or settlement obligations begin
- A fallback plan if delivery or your business requirements change

Early commitment may improve choice or terms, but those outcomes are not guaranteed. It can also lock you into a property before design, approvals or your own future requirements are settled. Your solicitor, accountant and other relevant advisers should review the commitment with you.

The selling and leasing agents on these projects do a professional job, but they act for the developer or landlord. That's their role.

We act only for you, the tenant or buyer. We help you:

- **Furnish It:** supply and install the furniture for your new space.

## Frequently asked questions

### What new commercial property is coming to Newcastle in 2027 and 2028?
Projects to investigate for a 2027/28 premises plan include The Commonage industrial units in Lambton, Hamilton Healthcare Hub and the refurbishment at 364-366 Hunter Street. These are marketed or proposed projects, not a confirmed schedule of completions. Confirm approvals, current availability and delivery dates with the relevant agent or project team.

### Why can limited new supply affect commercial rents and prices?
Supply is one influence on negotiating conditions, alongside demand, location, building quality, vacancy and transaction terms. Limited new supply does not establish that every property's rent or value will rise.

### How far ahead should I plan a commercial lease or purchase?
A 12 to 24 month planning window can be useful for a significant move, particularly if new development, approvals or a substantial fitout is involved. The right lead time depends on the actual project and your contractual deadlines.

### What is a pre-commitment lease?
It is an agreement to lease premises before the building is finished. Review the design, landlord works, approvals, incentives, access dates, rent commencement and delay provisions with your solicitor. Early commitment does not guarantee the best price or incentives.

### Is buying an industrial unit off the plan in Newcastle a good idea?
That depends on the business brief, funding, contract and risks. Check proposed use, areas, deposit arrangements, delivery conditions, strata costs and finance with the appropriate independent advisers before committing.

### Who are industrial units in Lambton suited to?
Colliers markets The Commonage for owner-occupiers and investors with warehouse, showroom and business-unit configurations. Suitability for a particular trade, storage or other business depends on the selected premises, permitted use and required approvals.

### Should I lease or buy my business premises?
Compare cash flow, capital requirements, flexibility, the property brief and transaction risks. Ownership exposes you to capital gains or losses and holding costs; leasing creates contractual occupancy and exit obligations. Seek independent legal, accounting and financial advice for your circumstances.

### What does a tenant representative do?
A tenant representative acts for the business seeking premises, helping define the brief, compare available options and negotiate commercial terms alongside the client's solicitor. YOS acts for the tenant or buyer under the agreed engagement, rather than the landlord or selling agent.

**Ready to plan your next move?** Whether you're eyeing a shed in Lambton, a suite in Hamilton or something in the CBD, the earlier you start, the more options you have. [Talk to our team today](/tenant-rep).

This article is general information only and is not financial, legal or tax advice.
